audit.whatIsWrong: Null Sphere is described as a silence in late and wants.foe[2]; Nether Blade is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's Null Sphere text: damage, interrupts channels, and a magic-damage shield on himself - no silence. Gwen has no channel that matters, so his Q does not deny her Hallowed Mist, which a silence would; believing otherwise makes you hold W you could have spent. Nether Blade carries autoReset on a 7s cooldown and restores mana, so his empowered swing arrives on the attack wind-up and his mana problem is smaller than the page assumes.
audit.corrected: late and wants.foe[2] now describe the Null Sphere shield and channel interrupt; early and mid name Nether Blade as the 7s reset that also refunds his mana.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen both item stages, contradicting whys[5] and whys[6].
audit.why: whys[5] says his Tear and Rod of Ages stacks start to out-tempo the two-item spike and whys[6] says he out-scales her outright. The lane is a hard early win that decays.
audit.corrected: Gwen / Gwen / Gwen / Gwen / Skill / Kassadin / Kassadin.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk is called 'a short, low-cooldown blink' three times with no number, and whys[3] describes level 6 while sitting in the levels 4-5 slot.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds - at rank 3 it is a two-second blink, which is why 'bait the R' stops being a plan late rather than merely getting harder. Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and Null Sphere 9s. Naming 5s and 2s is what separates the level-6 window you can still win from the two-item game you cannot.
audit.corrected: mid, late, whys[3] and spikes[1].text now carry the real Riftwalk numbers, and whys[3] is rewritten to describe levels 4-5 instead of level 6.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest early champs in the game and you punish that hard — he has no waveclear and no mobility until Riftwalk at 6, so shove the wave with Snip Snip! and E in to snip him every time he walks up for a last hit. Your %-max-HP Q out-trades him and the center snip's true damage cuts straight through his passive magic-damage reduction, while Skip 'n Slash refunds its cooldown on hit so you can poke and reposition for free. Don't overextend chasing — just deny CS, take an early plate, and stack the lead, because all he can do back is eat poke and pray for level 6.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest early champs in the game and you punish that hard — he has no waveclear and no mobility until Riftwalk at 6, so shove with Snip Snip! and E in to snip him every time he walks up for a last hit. Your %-max-HP Q out-trades him and the centre snip's true damage cuts through his passive magic reduction, while Skip 'n Slash refunds on hit so you poke and reposition for free. His one answer is Nether Blade, a 7s auto reset that also refunds his mana, so read the swing wind-up. Deny CS, take a plate, stack the lead.

edits.before: At 6 the lane changes character: Riftwalk is a short, low-cooldown blink that lets him hop out the instant you commit E-W-Q, so the clean all-ins you landed at levels 1-5 stop connecting for free. Your answer is to fight inside Hallowed Mist and bait the blink — make him burn R to escape, then catch the Needlework slow once he's grounded and out of mana. You still edge the straight duel through your two-item spike if you catch him with R down or before his Tear and Rod of Ages stacks finish, so keep forcing trades and shoving for plates. This is your last window to convert the early lead before he goes even and then ahead.
edits.after: At 6 the lane changes character: Riftwalk is a 5s blink at rank 1 that lets him hop out the instant you commit E-W-Q, so the clean all-ins you landed at 1-5 stop connecting for free. Your answer is to fight inside Hallowed Mist and bait the blink — make him burn R, then catch the Needlework slow while it is down and his mana is gone. You still edge the straight duel through your two-item spike if you catch him with R down or before his Tear and Rod of Ages finish, so keep forcing trades and shoving for plates. This is your last window to convert the early lead.

edits.before: This is where you lose — Kassadin is a hard scaler, and once he has Tear plus two AP items his Riftwalk goes near-spammable: he blinks in, silences with Q, dumps Force Pulse, and bursts you before your passive autos can grind him down. You can't pin him; Hallowed Mist's untargetability doesn't matter once he simply blinks the moment your damage starts, and the front of your Q gets softened by his magic reduction. Your only path is the lead you built before 6 — if the lane was even at first item, accept you'll be kited, give him no solo kills, and let your team peel him while you splitpush and shred their frontline elsewhere.
edits.after: This is where you lose — Kassadin is a hard scaler, and once he has Tear plus two AP items Riftwalk drops to 2s and goes near-spammable: he blinks in, shields himself on Null Sphere, dumps Force Pulse, and bursts you before your passive autos can grind him down. You cannot pin him; Hallowed Mist's untargetability stops mattering once he simply blinks the moment your damage starts, and the front of your Q gets softened by his magic reduction. Your only path is the lead you built before 6 — if the lane was even at first item, accept you will be kited, give him no solo kills, and splitpush while your team peels him.

edits.before: Riftwalk comes online and his blink dodges your E-W-Q — bait the R inside Hallowed Mist rather than forcing a clean Needlework fan.
edits.after: Still no Riftwalk until 6, so he stays escape-less — keep shoving and punish every last hit, but respect his 7s Nether Blade reset.

edits.before: Riftwalk (R) is a low-cooldown blink that lets him hop out of your E-W-Q the instant you commit — fight inside Hallowed Mist and bait the blink instead of forcing a clean fan of Needlework.
edits.after: Riftwalk (R) is a 5s blink at rank 1 that lets him hop out of your E-W-Q the instant you commit — fight inside Hallowed Mist and bait the blink rather than forcing a clean fan of Needlework.

edits.before: Tear plus two AP items turn Riftwalk into a spammable blink-Q-Force-Pulse burst — he silences with Q, blinks before your passive grinds him, and out-ranges your pin, so the lane is his.
edits.after: Tear plus two AP items drop Riftwalk to 2s and turn it into a spammable blink-Force-Pulse burst — he shields on Null Sphere, blinks before your passive grinds him, and out-ranges your pin.

edits.before: Use Riftwalk (R) to blink out of your E-W-Q all-in and bleed your Hallowed Mist timer before re-engaging on his terms
edits.after: Use a 5s Riftwalk to blink out of your E-W-Q all-in and bleed your Hallowed Mist timer before re-engaging on his terms

edits.before: Reach 2+ items where his Q-silence-into-blink-burst combo deletes you faster than your %-HP autos can grind him down
edits.after: Reach 2+ items where a 2s Riftwalk into Force Pulse burst deletes you faster than your %-HP autos can grind him down

notes: Three fixes. (1) FACTUAL: the page says Kassadin 'silences with Q' twice. Null Sphere does not silence - Riot's text is that it deals damage, INTERRUPTS CHANNELS, and shields him against magic damage. For a Gwen that difference is the whole plan: a silence would lock out Hallowed Mist, an interrupt does not, so you are not actually denied your mist when he blinks in. Corrected. (2) The chart gave Gwen both item stages while whys[5] and whys[6] say his Tear and Rod of Ages stacks out-tempo her and that she cannot pin a champion who blinks on demand; corrected to Gwen/Gwen/Gwen/Gwen/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin. I kept Gwen at levels 4-5 rather than the packet's 'Skill', because Riftwalk does not exist until 6 and both early and whys[1] say he has no mobility before then - whys[3] is written about level 6 while sitting in the levels 4-5 slot, which is why the chart drifted. (3) Nether Blade (W) is missing from the whole page: it is a 7s auto-attack reset that also restores his mana, so it is both his trade tell and the reason a poked-out Kassadin does not have to recall.
